transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm visiting today because I've been really struggling with focusing and paying attention to details, which has been causing me to make a lot of careless mistakes. I've also been feeling quite restless, and these issues have been going on for about 10 months now.
When you feel restless, is it more of a physical need to be constantly moving or fidgeting, or is it more of a mental feeling of being on edge and worried about the future?

It is definitely more of a physical restlessness. I feel this constant, uncomfortable urge to fidget, tap my feet, or just get up and walk around. It's not really about feeling worried or anxious about the future.
Beyond the physical restlessness, do you also find yourself frequently interrupting others, struggling to wait your turn, or acting impulsively without considering the consequences?

No, I don't really find myself doing those things. I don't think I have trouble waiting my turn or interrupting others, and I wouldn't say I act impulsively. It is mostly just the physical restlessness and the focus issues that I struggle with.
Do you often find that you lose things necessary for tasks, such as keys, wallets, or paperwork, or do you frequently become easily distracted by unrelated external stimuli?

No, I don't particularly struggle with losing important items like my keys or wallet, nor do I really notice being easily distracted by external noises or my surroundings. My main issues are more about forgetting daily chores or appointments, and really struggling to sustain my attention on tasks once I get started.
Did you experience these difficulties with sustaining attention and forgetfulness consistently throughout your childhood, or did these symptoms only emerge within the last year?

Although these struggles have been much more prominent and difficult to manage over the last 10 months, they aren't entirely new. I actually remember having similar issues with attention and forgetfulness back in childhood, definitely well before I was 12 years old.
